title: Smoother lease-based queueing and proactive KV prefetch policy for continuous batcher
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improves continuous batcher fairness and reduces KV miss tail latency by introducing lease smoothing and a proactive KV prefetch policy. Backward compatible runtime config with default off for private deployments.
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching can suffer starvation and tail latency spikes when a small number of long-running KV-heavy requests repeatedly seize batch slots. This PR introduces a lease-smoothing admission layer and a lightweight proactive KV prefetch policy to reduce starvation and lower p95/p99 latency without increasing average token cost.

Summary of changes: Added a lease-smoothing coordinator that softens immediate slot reclamation by introducing a short, jittered secondary lease window. Implemented a two-tier queue (fast-path / steady-path) to prefer short requests while ensuring long requests make progress. Added heuristics-based proactive KV prefetch: when a request is admitted and the model indicates KV-dependency (cacheable context patterns), we issue a low-overhead async prefetch for top-k KV shards to warm the cache before generation proceeds.

Key behaviors and knobs: - lease_smoothing_window_ms (default 12ms): small grace window applied after primary lease expiry; jitter added to avoid synchrony. - two_tier_threshold_tokens (default 64): requests under this length are routed to fast-path queue. - kv_prefetch_mode: off|heuristic|aggressive (default heuristic). - prefetch_shard_budget: number of KV shards to prefetch (default 3). - backpressure_decay_ms: controls how quickly soft reservations decay when reshuffling.

Why this is different: Rather than hard preemption or strict priority which can starve long requests, lease-smoothing preserves forward progress with minimal latency cost. Proactive KV warming is conservative: it only prefetches when a high-probability KV dependency is detected (pattern-based and model-provided hints) to avoid unnecessary IO.

Performance: Microbenchmarks on a 4-GPU staging cluster (gpus with 32GB) with mixed workload (60% short interactive, 40% long KV-heavy streaming): - median request latency: +1% (negligible) - p95 generation latency: -12% - p99 generation latency: -18% - observed KV miss penalty (measured as additional per-request stall ms): -35% - sustained throughput under 90th percentile latency SLO improved by ~8% in steady-state.

Safety and rollout: Feature gated by config flags, default enabled on hosted main but disabled in the private installer until customers opt in. Backwards-compatible defaults chosen to avoid regressions. Rolling deploy plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks on p99 and KV miss rate.

Testing: - Unit tests for lease expiry/jitter logic and queue routing. - Integration test harness that simulates mixture of KV-heavy and short requests with an emulated KV store. - Load tests against benchmark-lab with and without prefetch to validate throughput and cost impact. - Nightly perf regression alert added to catch delta >5% on p95.

Related: builds on ideas in ENG-7321 (fairness rebalancer) and ENG-7409 (kv warmup hints). Also references perf canary scripts updated in this PR.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Benchmark runs and numbers attached - [x] Docs: runtime config pages updated - [x] Migration notes added for private installer

Notes for reviewers: focus on the lease jitter distribution (exponential backoff vs uniform jitter), the heuristic condition for issuing KV prefetch, and performance cost trade-offs in aggressive prefetch mode.

notes_for_ops: Default behavior enabled on hosted only. Private installer keeps kv_prefetch_mode=off. If customers see increased KV store load after enabling aggressive prefetch, reduce prefetch_shard_budget to 1 or set kv_prefetch_mode=heuristic. Canary script provided at examples/deploy/canary-rollout.sh.
migration_instructions: No DB schema changes. To enable in private deployments modify serving.runtime kv_prefetch_mode and lease_smoothing_window_ms in runtime_config.yaml then restart runtime service. Recommended gradual ramp: 1%, 10%, 50% over 24h windows.
testing_summary: Unit and integration tests added. Load tests in benchmark-lab reproduced latency improvements and safe throughput gains. Nightly perf regression monitor added to tools/perf_alerts/p99_guard.yml.
